items.title: GitHub's releases/latest and the main branch both stood at v1.1.0: every v1.1.1-v1.1.88 release was a prerelease, so an install by the manifest got code 110 commits old
items.old_state: addressed by the 1.2.0 release ('Status after this review', AUDIT-1.1.88.md:197-199): main carries the released code and 1.2.0 was published as a stable release
items.evidence: Local main, origin/main and the tag v1.2.118 are one commit, b5a29e73 (git rev-parse); module.json:5 says 1.2.118 and module.json:68-69 point the manifest and the download at releases/latest/download. release.yml:101-109 refuses a dispatch from any ref but main, :247-250 publishes with --latest (or --prerelease on a train) at the dispatching commit. Read from GitHub through this session's connector on 20.11.2026: releases/latest is v1.2.118, target_commitish b5a29e7362932754d0f8aa7c11b986fe7a8dcafc, prerelease false, published 2026-11-19T11:59:07Z, assets module.json and module.zip; the eight newest releases (v1.2.111 to v1.2.118) are all prerelease false.
items.pinned_by: no test; release.yml:255-276 ('Show what latest resolves to') only warns when latest is not the tag; `node tools/check.mjs stamps notes --release <tag>` (release.yml:197) holds the tag to module.json
items.refutation_tried: Looked for both causes of the old failure today: main behind the newest tag (they are equal) and a release left as a prerelease (none of the eight newest is). Also read whether latest may lag by design: it may, between the two dispatches of a train (next field).
items.note: By decision, a train is first published as a prerelease and promoted to latest after the owner's smoke at a table (release.yml:50-66 and :278-318; the release rules file, step 8; the owner's O1 of 15.10.2026, INFRA I10 of 18.10.2026), so latest lagging the newest tag for that interval is intended, and the run warns. The brief said GitHub's API could not be reached; it could, read-only, and two calls were made (the latest release; the eight newest releases). Not read: the published module.json asset's own download field, which release.yml:211-226 rewrites to the tag's zip. Of the numbers v1.2.0 to v1.2.118 four have no tag in this clone (1.2.6, 1.2.28, 1.2.29, 1.2.43; 115 tags of 119); 1.2.43 has a notes file and the commit 35dc48d0.

items.title: The killer's (and the accomplice's) identity was readable from any player's console: the world setting murderState carried killerId and thirdId, and world settings reach every browser
items.old_state: left open at 1.2.0 on purpose ('Status after this review'); decided 02.09.2026 (Q16: fix with a GM-side ledger) and done 03.09.2026 for both the incident's cast and the Blackened register (AUDIT-1.2.13 'Stan realizacji' row 1b, in v1.2.14, commit 5c69acf2); the 1.2.42 audit called it half done (CASE-02, -03, -04)
items.evidence: Closed: the world setting murderState (settings.mjs:2840-2846) may hold only `active` and `stage` (incident-store.mjs:148-151 PUBLIC_INCIDENT; splitIncident :159-167 sends any other field to the cast or nowhere; world-secrets.mjs, murderState `only: [active, stage]`). The names live in the GMs' store castStore (gm-stores.mjs:429-431; client setting, settings.mjs:2904-2910), each participant holds a stamped copy (castCopy, gm-stores.mjs:554-557; settings.mjs:2912-2918), the chapter's killers are the GMs' blackenedStore (gm-stores.mjs:468-470; settings.mjs:2926-2931), and a bystander's incidentCast() is empty (settings.mjs:3535-3544). Still there by another road: mask-gm.mjs:424-426 and :443-455 write the token flag `veiled` on every token of a direct murder's killer and of a third on the killers' side (veilWanted :411-414) while the opening waits (murder-rules.mjs:548-551), and maskPatch (mask-gm.mjs:78-81) leaves the '?' token its actorId; token documents reach every browser.
items.pinned_by: The closed half: R9 (tier 0), R190 (tier 1), R191 (tier 0), R171 (tier 0), scenarios 11-killer-secrecy and 72-canary; R9, R190, R191 and R171 ok in tiers 0-1 of the central base run on b5a29e73 (20.11.2026: 1776 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped; read in the run's log). The open half is held as a known leak, not as a pass: scenario 21-masked-killer.mjs:230-232 (knownLeak foundry-veiled-token-actor) and 30-security.mjs:7020 (foundry-masked-token-actor) are expected red, and each fails the run when the reading stops reproducing.
items.still_wrong: A player whose student is not in the incident lists the tokens carrying flags['danganronpa-rpg'].veiled (or the token named '?' with the flag masked) in the console and reads game.actors.get(token.actorId).name: the killer of a direct murder, and a third seated on the killers' side, while the opening waits and for as long as a mask stands.
items.refutation_tried: Looked for a guard on the token road: visibility.mjs only stops the drawing; world-secrets.mjs has no rule for the token flags veiled or masked; a victim's and a bystander's cast copies hold no killer and the GMs' veil store reaches no player (scenario 21's checks beside the red one). Looked for the owner's decision: README.md:298-304 states both readings; the mask's sentence carries 'the owner's yes of 14.11.2026' (.github/release-notes/v1.2.113.md:187-189); for the veil's mark I found the coordinator's default (docs/dev/e112v/DESIGN.md:51-66, 'Asked of the coordinator as Q1') and the release notes' Known gaps, not an owner's answer.
items.note: By decision for the mask's half ('a curtain, not a wall', the owner's yes of 14.11.2026); a recorded Foundry limit for the veil's half (audit/harness/known-leaks.json rows foundry-masked-token-actor, since 1.2.113, and foundry-veiled-token-actor, since 1.2.116, narrowed in 1.2.118; class metadata, severity info). That the flag reaches a victim's and a bystander's browser is the harness's measurement written in that row (E112v, 16.11.2026, on dd9a56ed); I ran nothing. Severity major, as the 1.2.42 audit weighed the same kind of reading (CASE-03, CASE-04): it needs a console, which is why 1.1.88 called its own finding high and not critical. Counted once here; A5 below is the world setting alone.

items.title: forced-roll.mjs replaced the client's one dice generator (CONFIG.Dice.randomUniform) from the configuration hook until the next chat message, so any other roll on that client in between took the loaded sequence
items.old_state: narrowed to one roll on 03.09.2026 (third round of the verification; commit 5c69acf2): the swap sits on that roll instance's own evaluate and is lifted in a finally; tried live in the sandbox the same day
items.evidence: Gone: the open-ended window. forced-roll.mjs:176-226 shadows `evaluate` on the one Roll instance, swaps the generator only inside that call (:197-217) and restores it in `finally` (:219-224); once per purchase (`spent`, :177, :190-196). Still so: the generator swapped is the client's global one, for as long as one roll evaluates, and since E29 a second site does the same for the roller's copy of a roll the GM drew (roll-draw.mjs:637-650, the swap at :642-648).
items.pinned_by: R1537 (tier 0: both swaps are rows of the contract register; ok in tiers 0-1 of the central base run on b5a29e73 (20.11.2026: 1776 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped; read in the run's log)); tier 2 E15-T7 and E16-T35 read the loaded die's faces. No test found that evaluates a second roll inside the first's evaluation.
items.still_wrong: On one client, a second roll evaluated while a loaded roll's (or a drawn roll's copy's) evaluate is still pending would draw from the swapped generator and could take the forced face; whether an evaluation can stay pending that long on Foundry 14 was not established.
items.refutation_tried: Read what the window now spans: Daggerheart's buildEvaluate awaits `roll.evaluate()` and nothing else (the harness's verbatim copy, audit/harness/lib/dh-dice/dice/dhRoll.mjs:114-123), so with the default dice method no click can land inside it; forced-roll.mjs:45-48 says the same. Foundry's own evaluate is not in the repository, so a dice method that waits for a person was not read.
items.note: The 1.2.13 audit's own proposal (hand the values to the roll's own terms, no global hook) was not taken; the narrowing was. LIVE-E16-06 (9.2 item 305) is the open table reading for a non-default dice method.

new_observations.title: A Direct Murder declared in an Eclipse marks its declarer's tokens for every browser even when the lights then cancel it
new_observations.what: At an Eclipse's end the primary GM writes the token flag `veiled` on the tokens of every character with a declaration (veilAtTheLights -> veilActor -> token.update), before the lights judge. A declaration cancelled there (nobody in the room, a witness, a second declaration, a GM's refusal at the lights: eclipse.mjs:943-977) keeps the flag until lightsJudged runs after the whole judgement, which includes a GM's answer when one is asked (eclipse.mjs:973). A console on any player's browser that watches token updates reads who planned a murder that never opened. The declarations themselves left world data in E05 C3 for this reason (settings.mjs:899-909), and the known-leak row and the README sentence speak only of an opening that waits.

new_observations.title: The two known-leak rows that give a direct murder's killer are filed as metadata of severity info, under a file whose own rule says the killer's identity may not be deferred
new_observations.where: audit/harness/known-leaks.json: 'about' (D27) and the rows foundry-masked-token-actor and foundry-veiled-token-actor
new_observations.what: Both rows describe a console resolving a token to the killer's actor and name; both are classed `metadata` / `info` with a `foundryLimit`. The class decides how the record is read later (from 1.3.0 'only foundryLimit and deferred entries remain'). The mask's reading has the owner's yes of 14.11.2026; for the veil's I found none.

new_observations.title: The class of defect A1 was has no guard: the lint holds four rules and no-dupe-keys is not one
new_observations.what: A repeated key in an object literal still loads silently. Measured today with a script over scripts/ (271 files parsed with espree, 53,556 object literals): 0 repeated static keys, so nothing is wrong now; nothing would say so when one arrives.

not_established: A4: whether a roll's evaluate on Foundry 14 can stay pending while a person acts (a dice method that asks for the faces), which is what would let a second roll on the same client draw from the swapped generator (forced-roll.mjs:197-221, roll-draw.mjs:642-648). Foundry's source is not in the repository; LIVE-E16-06 at a table with a non-default dice method, with a second roll thrown meanwhile, would settle it.

A9: what another player's screen draws while a token is dragged in an Eclipse on Foundry 14.370. No reading exists in docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md or docs/dev/e39/CALIBRATION.md; LIVE-E116-01 and -02 (9.2 items 558, 559) would settle it.
